newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open mostly weaker amid soft dollar.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open mostly weaker amid soft dollar.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mostly weaker on Thursday as further weakness in the Canadian dollar weighed on most parts of the T-bill yield curve, dealers said.

"It's currency driven. The merchandise trade came in a little weaker than expected. It's just a pullback," said a dealer with one bank-owned brokerage. "You've got fundamentals going against you here."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.23 percent from 2.21 percent at the close of trading on Wednesday.

Canada's dollar opened weaker in heavy trading at C$1.3992 (US$0.7146) after reaching a two-year low of C$1.4018 (US$0.7133) in overnight trade. The unit weakened from the open after the release of the Canadian merchandise trade surplus for Feburary.
The merchandise trade surplus widened in February to C$2.19 million. A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of C$2.35 billion in February.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.56 percent from 3.51 percent on Wednesday.
The one-year T-bill softened to yield 4.27 percent from 4.21 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.10 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
